headline: Mills asks Congress for more Maine heating aid as oil prices stay near records
dek: The governor says current LIHEAP funding does not reflect sharply higher fuel costs, while Maine's latest survey puts heating oil at $5.96 a gallon after a record $6.02.
body: Maine's heating-cost story took a new turn Friday when Gov. Janet Mills asked Congress to provide supplemental funding for the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program. In a letter to U.S. Sens. Susan Collins and Angus King and Reps. Chellie Pingree and Jared Golden, Mills said the federal money set aside for the winter does not reflect the higher fuel prices now facing Maine and other cold-weather states. Her request is a call for Congress to act, not an approved increase in benefits. The governor's announcement is at https://www.maine.gov/governor/mills/news/governor-mills-calls-congress-boost-liheap-funding-2026-10-02.

The request follows a record heating-oil price in Maine. The Maine Department of Energy Resources says its statewide cash-price survey was $5.96 per gallon on September 28, after reaching a record $6.02 the previous week. The latest average is down slightly from the peak but remains far above the $3.33 average reported for the same time last year, according to Bangor Daily News' account of the state data. DOER's survey covers delivered-fuel retailers and warns that local prices can be higher or lower; it is not a guaranteed price for every customer. The current table is at https://www.maine.gov/energy/heating-fuel-prices.

The difference is consequential for a household that needs a full 275-gallon tank. Mills' office says the record price adds about $740 to that fill compared with a year earlier. Bangor Daily News reported that this week's $5.96 average is nearly 80% above last year's level, with prices ranging from $5 to $6.30 in the state's latest regional breakdown. Those figures describe spot cash prices, so pre-buy contracts, discounts, delivery fees and a home's actual consumption can produce a different bill.

The new federal request builds on an earlier projection rather than replacing it. WMTW News 8, citing the National Energy Assistance Directors Association, reported September 29 that average Maine heating-oil spending could reach $2,939 during the 2026-27 heating season, 77% above the $1,664 comparison figure for last winter. That is a regional estimate, not a promise that every oil-heated home will spend the same amount. Weather, insulation, thermostat settings, building size, equipment efficiency and the price charged by a local supplier will all affect an individual household's costs. Homes heated with propane, wood, electricity or natural gas face different price patterns.

Mills' letter describes the risk as especially acute in Maine because roughly half of the state's homes rely on heating oil as their primary fuel and many rural homes are older. A larger fuel bill can compete with food, rent, transportation and medical expenses, while a household with little fuel left may have limited ability to wait for a better price. The governor said Congress should make more LIHEAP money available quickly; the letter does not identify a specific supplemental dollar amount or guarantee that lawmakers will approve one.

Maine has also begun other forms of assistance. The Mills administration said October 1 that eligible low-income households will be automatically enrolled in a $40 million expansion of electric-bill discounts through SupportLink and the Low Income Assistance Program. The governor's office says discounts for Central Maine Power customers can range from 25% to 81% and for Versant customers from 17% to 83%, depending on income; households served by smaller consumer-owned utilities receive the benefit differently. The announcement is at https://www.maine.gov/governor/mills/news/governor-mills-announces-automatic-electric-bill-discounts-thousands-maine-families-2026-10-01.

For direct heating help, MaineHousing says eligible homeowners and renters can apply for the 2026-27 Home Energy Assistance Program, supported by federal LIHEAP funds. Applications opened in August and remain available until funds are exhausted. MaineHousing says crisis assistance for households with extremely low fuel supplies opens November 1 and requires a HEAP application first through a local Community Action Agency. Program details and income rules are at https://www.mainehousing.org/programs-services/Energy/energydetails/LIHEAP.

The immediate practical question for a Maine household is therefore not whether the $2,939 projection will come true, but whether help is available before a tank runs low. The governor is asking Congress to increase the federal pool; the state is directing eligible residents toward HEAP, electric-bill discounts and its updated 2026-27 Winter Heating Guide. Until Congress responds, households can compare the current local delivered-fuel price with the state's weekly benchmark and apply early, because both eligibility and available funds shape what assistance a household ultimately receives.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Mills seeks more Maine heating aid as oil prices rise
seoDescription: Maine Gov. Janet Mills is seeking more LIHEAP funding as heating oil prices remain near records and projected winter costs approach $2,939.
sourceName: Office of Governor Janet T. Mills
